passage: Note, Tuesday, by Jeevan, Science teacher. Preeti stayed back after the bell with three test papers folded in her bag. She spread them on my desk and pointed: the same type of question had lost her marks each time. Her family was thinking of a whole extra tuition course, and she said she was not sure it was what she needed. I suggested a doubt session twice a week, twenty minutes after school, where she brings only the questions she got wrong. She wrote the days in her diary at once, Tuesday and Thursday, and said, "That is what I actually need." I will look at her next paper to see whether it is working.

qa.q: How often did Preeti and Jeevan agree to meet?
qa.a: They agreed to meet twice a week, on Tuesday and Thursday, after school.

qa.q: What did Preeti feel about the full coaching batch?
qa.a: Unsure that it was what she needed, since she felt a targeted session fitted her problem better.

qa.q: What could Preeti do to get the most from the sessions?
qa.a: Bring specific wrong questions and try them first, because targeted help saves time.

qa.q: How might Preeti's family see the doubt sessions compared with a full batch?
qa.a: As a lighter and cheaper option aimed at the real gaps, though they may want to see results first.

grounding: A student shows her last three test papers to the teacher and agrees on twice-weekly doubt sessions instead of a full coaching batch.
